name: Arcturus Defense Solutions IronShepherd DACI-6 Automaton Com
description:
The IronShepherd DACI-6 is the most sophisticated Direct Automaton Control Interface ever produced for field deployment, engineered specifically for operators who command mixed formations of Iowan Behemoth-class autonomous combat machines and light drone swarms in coordinated combined-arms operations. The implant maintains six simultaneous high-bandwidth neural uplink channels to autonomous machines — each channel capable of sustaining full behavioral override, tactical repositioning, weapons release authorization, and real-time sensor feed integration for a formation of up to eight Behemoths per channel, yielding a theoretical maximum command authority over forty-eight Behemoth-class units simultaneously, alongside a dedicated swarm management layer handling up to 200 light drone units through distributed mesh-network coordination. The DACI-6's proprietary TactileSense feedback system translates the Behemoths' onboard sensor arrays into a compressed proprioceptive signal the operator perceives as a ghostly body-sense of each machine — operators describe knowing where each Behemoth is and what it perceives as instinctively as knowing the position of their own limbs. Quantum-encrypted command links operate on rotating keys with 800-millisecond refresh cycles, making signal interception and command spoofing effectively impossible within engagement timescales.

The IronShepherd DACI-6 has fundamentally altered the calculus of armored warfare in GLMZ's contested zones. A single DACI-6 operator embedded with a Behemoth formation can outperform entire conventional command-and-control networks, reacting to battlefield developments at neural speed and coordinating machine assets with a fluidity that no radio-based command structure can match. The implant has also generated profound philosophical unease in military ethics circles: operators who spend extended periods in deep DACI-6 immersion frequently report a blurring of self-identity, describing a sensation of being simultaneously human and machine, distributed across dozens of armored bodies. Arcturus officially classifies this phenomenon as 'Extended Formation Identification' and insists it is non-pathological, though independent neuropsychiatrists have published sharply contradicting assessments.
legality: Military-Only — Command authority over Behemoth-class machines restricted to credentialed military operators; unauthorized Behemoth control constitutes deployment of an autonomous weapons platform, a Class-S offense
installation_requirements: Full cranial surgical suite with dedicated automaton interface calibration rig; minimum 90-day post-installation Behemoth synchronization training; requires Tier 2+ existing neural mesh; Arcturus DACI Division-certified surgeon
rejection_risk: Moderate (18%) — Primary rejection risk concentrated in TactileSense feedback integration; candidates with prior phantom limb conditions face elevated complications
maintenance: Bi-monthly Behemoth firmware synchronization to maintain command protocol compatibility; quarterly quantum key stack servicing; annual TactileSense recalibration to prevent feedback drift

side_effects: Extended Formation Identification syndrome — operators lose subjective boundaries between self and commanded machines during prolonged immersion, requiring structured decompression protocols after operations exceeding 6 hours

Phantom formation sense persisting after disconnection — operators continue to perceive the positional status of their last commanded Behemoth formation for hours or days post-operation, experienced as spectral presences in peripheral awareness
Compulsive tactical assessment of environments — operators involuntarily calculate optimal Behemoth deployment patterns for every physical space they enter, even in civilian contexts
Documented cases of operators experiencing genuine grief responses upon the destruction of commanded Behemoth units, despite full cognitive awareness that the machines are not living beings
cultural_context: Behemoth handlers running DACI-6 implants occupy a unique and somewhat isolated niche in GLMZ's military culture. Their peers regard them with a mixture of awe and wariness — the sight of a single operator standing motionless in a command position while dozens of multi-ton autonomous war machines move with eerie coordinated precision is viscerally unsettling even to hardened combat veterans. Among themselves, DACI-6 operators have developed a quiet, contemplative culture centered on the paradox of their role: they are simultaneously the most powerful individuals on any battlefield and the most philosophically displaced, caught between human identity and the distributed machine-consciousness of their formations. The informal community is tight-knit and insular, sharing decompression techniques and identity-anchoring rituals through private channels accessible only through their implants.

story_hooks: A DACI-6 operator has gone missing during an operation, but their Behemoth formation is still moving — executing complex tactical maneuvers as if still being commanded, despite no detectable operator signal. Something else is controlling them, or the operator is alive and transmitting from somewhere impossible

The players are hired to extract a DACI-6 operator who has been captured by a rival faction attempting to use them as a living key to seize control of a Behemoth formation currently guarding a critical installation

A decommissioned DACI-6 implant is generating ghost command signals — echoes of its former operator's final battle — that are causing a mothballed Behemoth unit to spontaneously reactivate and replay fragments of a battle that officially never happened
